claims.text: Equiatomic as-cast FeCoNiTi exhibits a dual-phase microstructure.
The dual-phase FeCoNiTi microstructure contains ferromagnetic fcc and hexagonal C14 Laves phases.
Arc melting on a water-cooled Cu hearth provides rapid quenching that stabilizes the fcc+C14 dual-phase microstructure.
Fe27Co27Ni17Ti29 is a C14-dominant alloy variant.
The fcc phase has an approximate composition of Fe21.3Co24.8Ni32.2Ti21.6.
The C14 phase has an approximate composition of Fe27.3Co26.6Ni17.4Ti28.7.
Coexistence and chemical segregation of the fcc and C14 phases create interfaces that enhance domain-wall pinning.
The Fe, Co, and Ni sublattice couples antiferromagnetically to the Ti sublattice in the fcc phase.
Antiferromagnetic sublattice coupling reduces saturation magnetization.
Antiferromagnetic sublattice coupling reinforces ferromagnetic ordering up to approximately 1084 K.
Orbital contributions, the presence of the C14 phase, and spin-canted interfacial structures increase coercivity through enhanced domain-wall pinning.
The dual-phase alloy will have a coercive field approaching 667 Oe at 400 K.
Single-phase fcc Fe-Co-Ni high-entropy alloys have coercive fields below 100 Oe.
Single-phase fcc Fe-Co-Ni high-entropy alloys have minimal orbital-moment contributions.
The dual-phase alloy will display distinct magnetic ordering transitions near 168 K and 1084 K.
Pure single-phase fcc or pure C14 alloys will not show the same magnitude of coercivity enhancement as the dual-phase alloy.
Pure single-phase fcc or pure C14 alloys will not show the same multi-transition magnetic behavior as the dual-phase alloy.
The magnitude of the coercivity increase may vary with the dual-phase structure and chemical segregation produced during quenching.
Failure to exceed 100 Oe substantially at 400 K or failure to show the specified magnetic transitions is defined as falsifying the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The initial state is already described as an as-cast dual-phase FeCoNiTi alloy, while the intervention is defined as rapid quenching during synthesis to stabilize that same dual-phase state. This leaves no clearly distinct pre-intervention material state.
The Fe27Co27Ni17Ti29 C14-dominant variant is called compositionally matched to equiatomic FeCoNiTi, although its stated elemental proportions differ substantially, especially for Ni and Ti.

Magnetic measurements are limited to 400 K, but the experiment and falsification rule require identification of a transition near 1084 K. That transition cannot be directly tested over the stated measurement range.

The baseline is an fcc Fe-Co-Ni alloy without stated Ti content, yet the design treats it as the reference for FeCoNiTi. It is therefore not clearly compositionally matched, so composition and phase constitution are confounded.
